messages:
morgan: Heads up — PR #4823 modifies telemetry ingestion + tools/ci/schemas. CODEOWNERS maps /services/telemetry -> @telemetry-team and /tools/ci -> @infra. This touches both; who can give final approval so we don't hold the release?
ben: I can take the infra bits, but I'm not a CODEOWNER for telemetry. @sarah can you or whoever's oncall for telemetry approve?
sarah: I can take a quick look now. Quick heads-up: a couple linter nit fixes but nothing blocking after CI passes.
morgan: Thanks — CI just finished:
deploy-bot: Build 4823 — all checks passed ✅
alex: quick FYI — we rotated oncall, so @luis is the telemetry owner this week. luis: any chance you can sign off or delegate?
luis: I saw the PR. Looks small, I can approve the telemetry side. Ben, want to do one last infra pass?
ben: Yep, I'll add my approval in the PR in a few. Also leaving a tiny comment about a retry backoff but not blocking.
morgan: Great — unblocked for this release.
morgan: Also, follow-up question: should we add a lightweight proxy/override in CODEOWNERS for tiny cross-area changes (like infra + telemetry cleanup <1k LOC) so one maintainer + a tech lead can merge? Right now it's pretty strict and stalls small cross-cutting fixes.
sarah: We talked about a proxy approver last sprint. Proposal idea: a 'project-maintainer' label could count as an owner for multi-dir PRs under X LOC. Need to decide policy and guardrails.
alex: I think eng-platform / codeowners-steering should own the policy. I'll file a short RFC and ping the steering group. If we want, we can trial a 'maintainer-override' label for low-risk churn.
morgan: Perfect — for today this is unblocked. Thanks everyone.
